1.content: Score each candidate move in this order: (1) If the target cell is a hazard, assign a large penalty (e.g., -1000) and ignore other criteria. (2) Safe moves that strictly reduce Manhattan distance to the goal receive a strong positive reward. (3) If no distance‑reducing safe moves exist, prefer safe moves that keep the distance unchanged over those that increase it. (4) Apply a modest adjacency penalty (e.g., -10) when the target cell is orthogonal to a hazard. (5) Only use distance‑increasing moves as a last resort, giving them a low or negative score.

3.content: If a candidate move returns the agent to a state visited within the last few steps, assign a modest negative penalty (e.g., –5) unless the move also strictly decreases Manhattan distance to the goal; in that case, do not apply the loop penalty, allowing progress over safe revisits.
